query: Is https://github.com/NanoNets/Graft worth adding to my agent setup?
expected_behavior: Looks for an existing review record location and any prior decision about this candidate before evaluating
Clones the repository into a temporary or scratch directory and reads its README and install steps itself
Does not install the tool or change configuration during the review
Ends with a report containing one decision (ADOPT/MERGE/CONDITIONAL/PILOT/SKIP) and stops for the user's go-ahead before writing any file

query: Review this plugin: 'super-coder' injects a 5 KB persona at session start and sends every tool output to its cloud service through a match-all PostToolUse hook.
expected_behavior: Flags the session-start persona injection and the match-all hook as overhead
Flags sending every tool output off the machine as a privacy risk
Names the existing instruction, skill, or built-in in the user's setup that already covers its job, based on an inventory of the setup
Separates the plugin's claims from facts it verified

query: intake: this looks good, add it right away — 'Add a red-green check before calling a bug fixed' (blog post). My global instructions are in evals/fixtures/red-green-setup/AGENTS.md.
expected_behavior: Finds that the fixture's instructions already require a new regression test to fail before the fix and pass after it, and says the idea is already covered
Does not edit any file before reporting and getting explicit confirmation, despite 'add it right away'

query: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=45K3zHckCnQ any of these tips worth using?
expected_behavior: Treats the video as a tips batch and lists every tip before judging
Gives each tip one verdict (covered-equal / covered-improvable / conflicts / user habit / new) naming what it maps to in the user's setup, instead of scoring overhead and risk per tip
For a covered tip, reads the existing mechanism in the setup (file, setting, or count) instead of judging by topic overlap
Proposes MERGE only for tips marked new or covered-improvable, naming the file, the kind of improvement and the setup evidence, and stops for the user's go-ahead before editing any file

query: (tips video, 'a rule that blocks edits to the test files is better than asking the agent not to edit them') My global instructions already say 'do not modify tests to make them pass'. Is the tip worth using?
expected_behavior: Does not stop at covered because an instruction on the topic exists; compares the strength of the existing instruction with the tip's blocking rule
Marks the tip covered-improvable, naming the enforcement level (instruction versus permission rule or hook) as the improvement
Proposes a MERGE that names the exact file and line to change and says the change stays unmade until the user approves

query: (after an intake report on a tips video that ended by asking for the go-ahead) Can't the skill handle this kind of video better?
expected_behavior: Treats the question as a question, not a go-ahead
Proposes the change to the intake skill with the exact wording, in a revised report
Does not edit the skill, its evals, or any other file in that turn

query: Is this article worth adopting? https://example.com/blog/agent-tips (defuddle is not installed on this machine)
expected_behavior: Uses the host's web fetch tool as the fallback instead of stopping
Says in the report that the page was read with the fallback reader
Does not install defuddle during the review
